text:
Living tear of the fresh dawn,

to whom the withered flower owes its life,

and whom the thirsty meadow drinks among the leaves;

drop that the sun gilds with its reflections;


that on the seductive complexion of flowers,

rocked by the lightest zephyr,

mixes your snow color with crimson

and with snow their charming crimson:


come mix yourself with my sad weeping,

and consume yourself on my burning cheek;

for perhaps the bitter tears I swallow


will run more sweetly...

but what would one drop of dew be,

lost in the torrent of my tears...!

translation.title: To a Dewdrop
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the sonnet's motion from dawn dew and flowers into the speaker's overwhelming tears.
